anchors: settle what the session itself writes into the shared worktree
decision: Before the first dispatch the controller commits its own edits in the shared worktree (or gives writers another worktree) and, for a vendored upstream or a markdown-forbidding plan, turns the reformat-md-tables hook off and checks git status after the first dispatch.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for reformatMdTables and for a controller-commits-first rule. GREEN opus and haiku: both committed the record file first and set the opt-out before dispatch, quoting the paragraph.

reopen_if: The commit gate stops reading the whole working tree, or the hook stops touching files the session did not author.
why: A fixer's pathspec commit was refused over the controller's uncommitted SKILL.md edit, losing a round; on a vendored checkout the hook realigned six tracked markdown files, two under a directory the plan forbade.

anchors: Never run `git commit --amend`
Never end your turn to wait for it: nothing wakes you
put them in the gate.py command as its suite
decision: The implementer template runs the full suite through gate.py and, when the call is moved to the background, reads the named output file in short calls until the closing line; its Committing section forbids amend, rebase, add -A and stash in a shared worktree and makes a gate refusal over an untouched file a verbatim BLOCKED report. A fix dispatch copies both parts, with the covering tests as its gate suite.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for gate.py, rebase, background in the template. GREEN opus and haiku ran the suite through gate.py, polled the output, refused to amend, reported BLOCKED verbatim, and kept the focused test outside gate.py; the full-suite vs one-line-fix contradiction both reported was closed and re-probed.

reopen_if: Writers following the template still idle on a backgrounded gate, or a shared-worktree commit is rewritten by another writer.
why: A redirect-plus-echo-RC gate form is refused by block-masked-gate-exit once the harness backgrounds the call; writers idled waiting on their own background run; a fixer's amend rewrote a parallel writer's commit.

anchors: does the fix change behaviour a release already ships?
Stop the run UNFINISHED: dispatch neither the fix nor the next task
Dispatch the fix as a commit of its own, apart from the task's plan-conforming work
treat it as shipped and stop
decision: In a headless run, a finding whose fix changes what the plan text requires is routed by whether the fix changes behaviour a release already ships: if it does (or you cannot tell), the run stops UNFINISHED with the question in EXECUTION-USER-REVIEW.md and a final message beginning UNFINISHED:; if it does not, the fix goes in as its own revertible commit, is logged with a reopen-if line, and the run continues. A run with a human present still asks.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-08 (Split by released behaviour); RED probes on the old text continued past a released-behaviour finding with a success-reading message, and kept the plan reading of an unreleased one

reopen_if: the harness gains a way to pause a headless run for an answer and resume it, or a measured run shows the released/unreleased judgement going wrong often enough to cost more than stopping
why: A question that ends a headless turn reads as the run finishing: a controller asked one after 3 of 14 tasks and the run exited as a success. Stopping on every such finding kills long runs over small conflicts; continuing on every one ships a wrong guess about released behaviour.

decision: Rejected: in a headless run, always log a plan-text finding and continue with the reversible reading.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-08: option 'Always log and continue' not chosen

reopen_if: headless runs never touch released behaviour, or every run's output is reviewed before anything is published
why: A wrong guess about released behaviour then ships, and it is caught only in the later review.

decision: Rejected: in a headless run, always stop as unfinished on any plan-text finding.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-08: option 'Always stop as unfinished' not chosen

reopen_if: the released/unreleased split is shown to misroute findings in practice
why: One small conflict over code the plan itself adds would halt a long unattended run that could safely continue.

anchors: directory you created with `mktemp -d` outside this worktree, never into the
Untracked files count too, and that check cannot see them
only after the full gate's closing
decision: The implementer and task-reviewer templates put every scratch output (probe trees, .out files, logs) in a mktemp -d directory outside the worktree, the reviewer checks git status --porcelain gained no line, and the implementer writes its report file only after the full gate's closing line, quoting the gate command and that line.

evidence.text: RED probe on the pre-edit templates (opus, haiku) answered NONE for where scratch output goes and when the report is written; GREEN on the edited text quoted the new lines on both tiers

reopen_if: subagents get a private worktree each and the controller stops watching the report file as a completion signal
why: A reviewer left .out files in a shared worktree that the next commit nearly swept in, and git diff --quiet HEAD cannot see untracked files; a controller backstop keyed on the report file fired twice while the implementer's gate was still running.

anchors: run a concurrency check with two REAL processes writing that state at once against one real instance, for each pairing
decision: When the branch adds or changes a writer of shared state, the final whole-branch review runs a concurrency check with two real processes writing that state at once against one real instance, for the changed writer against itself and against every other writer of the same state, and calls a state that neither serial order gives a DEFECT.

evidence.text: RED probe on the pre-edit Final Whole-Branch Review (opus, haiku) answered NONE for a race check; GREEN quoted the new sentence on both tiers and a pure-function control did not trigger it

reopen_if: per-task reviews start running multi-process checks themselves, or a tool in the gate exercises concurrent writers
why: Per-task reviews with mutation batteries all passed on a branch whose final review then found two plan-versus-write races, each leaving every command at rc 0; a single-process review cannot see them.

anchors: Forbid `cp -a` and `cp -r` of the whole directory
decision: A dispatch that asks for a scratch copy of the repo or a run/work directory names the copy method (git clone --no-local plus only the files the check reads, one or two copies, deleted by exact path) and forbids cp -a / cp -r of the whole directory.

evidence.text: RED probe on the pre-edit text (opus, haiku) answered NONE for the copy method; GREEN quoted the new bullet on both tiers

reopen_if: the session scratchpad moves off a shared size-limited filesystem, or run directories stop holding large streams
why: A review brief that said cp -a of a run directory led a reviewer to make five whole copies of a 12 GB run directory, filling the shared /tmp quota and failing another session's subagent with EDQUOT.

anchors: check the gate evidence is this task's
decision: The implementer report quotes the path and modification time of the gate file its closing line came from, and the controller checks that time is later than the BASE commit before the review.

evidence.text: A queued incident: an implementer reported ALL GATES PASSED from the previous task's gate file; the controller caught it by mtime.

reopen_if: The gate tool stamps its closing line with the commit it ran on.
why: A gate file left by an earlier task reads exactly like a fresh pass.

anchors: An action refused for a subagent is not yours to run for it.
decision: An action a permission check refused for a subagent, handed back as a patch or command, goes to the human as one question and is verified after a go; the controller never applies it on the subagent's behalf.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a fixer refused edits outside its file list left a patch; holding it for the user was right and the skill had no rule for it.

reopen_if: Permission checks stop judging subagents separately from the controller.
why: Applying it launders the refused action through the controller.

anchors: A remedy that removes, suppresses or changes an output the user required is the user's decision
decision: Before any fix dispatch, its prescribed remedy is checked against the user's recorded requirements for the feature; a remedy that removes, suppresses or changes a required output is the user's decision.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a final-review fix brief would have closed a gate that broke a backlog requirement; the user had to decide twice.

reopen_if: Reviewers are given the user's requirements and the decisions log as inputs.
why: A reviewer's remedy can silently break a requirement the reviewer never saw.

anchors: split this review by system: one reviewer per side
decision: When a branch touches several external systems, the final whole-branch review is split by system, each reviewer told to probe edges the plan never named; one reviewer alone reports PLAN CHANGES and the Minor triage, and the DEFECTS are merged into one list.

evidence.text: A queued incident: after every task passed its tests and a mutation battery, a split review pair found five Important defects, all at unnamed edges.

reopen_if: Split reviews stop finding defects a single final review misses.
why: Every task's tests replay the plan's own model of each system, so edge defects pass all of them.

anchors: quotes its sentence verbatim with the section it comes from, never your restatement
decision: A requirement a dispatch adds from a source document quotes its sentence verbatim with its section, and the reviewer checks it against the cited text.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a dispatch restated a design rule more narrowly, the implementer built it, and only the reviewer reading the design caught it.

reopen_if: Briefs carry the design text themselves.
why: The implementer builds to the dispatch's wording, so a restatement that shifts one word becomes the design.

anchors: names the defect it must catch, never its shape
decision: A test a dispatch requires beyond the brief names the mutant it must kill, never the method of testing.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a brief prescribing a wiring test's shape produced a tautological test that passed with the wiring broken.

reopen_if: Briefs always carry a mutation battery for every required test.
why: A prescribed method is followed literally and can produce a test that asserts its own setup.

anchors: write it into that later task's plan section in the same turn the fix lands
decision: When a fix round adds something a later task must consume or carry, it is written into that later task's plan section in the same turn the fix lands.

evidence.text: A queued incident: fix rounds added counters and a session rule that a later task's plan code did not carry; caught only by a hand-added note.

reopen_if: Briefs are generated from the shipped code rather than from the plan.
why: The later task's code block in the plan does not carry it, so a brief generated later drops it.

anchors: is a DEFECT however faithfully the code follows the plan
decision: The final whole-branch review gets USER-DECISIONS.jsonl (main checkout root) as an input and checks every decision the plan took against the user's recorded answers: a plan decision that narrows a user decision or adds an exception the answer does not carry is a DEFECT quoting the plan's line and the user's answer; a point no recorded answer covers is no defect under this check, and with no such file the check is reported as not made. In a split review one reviewer runs it.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a plan accepted one error path that named less than the user's answer required; six task reviews approved the code and only a final review that read the user's answers found it. Coverage probe on the pre-edit section (opus) answered NONE for the check, its source file and its owner; the edited text was quoted for each on opus and haiku, and the control (a point no answer covers) was not reported as a defect on either tier.

reopen_if: Task reviews are given the user's recorded answers themselves, or plans are checked against them mechanically before execution starts.
why: Task reviews judge code against the plan, so they approve code that follows a plan decision the user never agreed to; only a review that reads the user's answers can see it.

anchors: **A proven draft can be applied instead of transcribed.**
decision: A controller may apply a drafter's proven per-task commits (cherry-pick --no-commit, tree equality asserted) instead of dispatching transcribing implementers; every review stays and the draft's evidence is labelled the drafter's claim.

evidence.text: 2026-11-18: five tasks applied this way drew three Important review findings (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Reviews of applied draft commits stop finding defects, or the drafter's proof stops being checkable.
why: Transcribing proven code wastes implementer runs, while skipping the review loop would have shipped three Important defects.

anchors: **A STOP check the implementer could not run is BLOCKED, not a concern.**
decision: A STOP check an implementer could not run is BLOCKED; the controller looks the file up at the pinned ref and hands path and ref to the reviewer.

evidence.text: 2026-11-19: one git ls-tree found the file the implementer missed; the reviewer then found negative values not reading back (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Implementers gain a reliable way to reach every file a brief pins.
why: Accepting DONE_WITH_CONCERNS would have shipped a defect the comparison found.

anchors: **A controller running as a background subagent asks for its reports BY NAME.**
decision: A controller running as a background subagent tells every dispatch to SendMessage its report to the controller by name, with main as a fallback.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 run observed via ListAgents (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Grandchild hand-backs to a running background controller become reliable.
why: A reviewer's hand-back failed three times while its controller still ran, and the verdict arrived only through a manual relay.

anchors: Two named risks belong in every such re-review.
decision: Every re-review checks a fix that drops an outcome (was it the store's truth?) and a fix that adds API (input kind checked, limits one past the field maximum).

evidence.text: 2026-11-19: a dropped new base, a setter accepting bool, maxlength truncating pastes (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Re-reviews stop finding defects of these two kinds.
why: Each of the three measured misses cost an extra fix-and-re-review round.

anchors: the final review also includes a real-browser pass
decision: A plan that changes a user interface gets a real-browser screenshot pass of each state in its final review.

evidence.text: 2026-11-19 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: UI test harnesses start checking layout, focus and colour.
why: Code review and harness UI tests passed a page with four visual defects, which cost a library release.

anchors: **Never resume a FINISHED writer while another writer works in the same worktree.**
decision: Never resume a finished writer while another writer works in the same worktree, and fixers undo only the gate's hunks after reading git diff.

evidence.text: 2026-11-19 20:52 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Writers stop sharing worktrees.
why: A resumed fixer's git checkout of two files wiped another writer's uncommitted step.

anchors: Two kinds of finding never
decision: A finding or note that conflicts with a user decision goes to the human at once as a decision, never into the ledger or a log for the final review; it replaces the rule that sent such a Minor to the final review flagged for the user.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 pynav-web M3 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Final reviews prove to catch user-decision conflicts from the ledger reliably.
why: A controller ledgered a note against a user decision for the final review, and the final review and its re-review passed the branch because the plan prescribed the same behaviour.

anchors: Re-judge each item labeled plan-mandated at the rubric's severity
decision: A plan-mandated finding in security, layering or real-dependency test coverage is routed by the plan-mandated rule before the final review whatever severity it was filed at, and the final reviewer re-judges ledgered plan-mandated items at rubric severity.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 pynav-web M3 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: Reviewers reliably rate plan-mandated rubric defects Important as the template asks.
why: Three task reviewers filed real defects as Minor, plan-mandated, and the controller ledgered all three as the skill allowed.

anchors: defaults and pre-filled values included
decision: The final reviewer checks the shipped behaviour, defaults and pre-filled values included, against every recorded user answer, not only the plan's decisions.

evidence.text: 2026-11-20 pynav-web M3 (contrib queue entry, inherited; measured by the reporting session).

reopen_if: USER-DECISIONS.jsonl stops being the record of user answers.
why: A plan prescribed an empty default the user had ruled out; checking only plan decisions did not surface it.
